contentHtml:
Dubai has become one of the world’s most attractive destinations for investors looking to secure residency while expanding their business footprint. With its strategic location, stable economy, and tax-friendly policies, the UAE offers a clear pathway for investors to settle and grow.

If you’re considering making Dubai your new base, understanding the investor visa cost in Dubai, the eligibility criteria, and the required documents is the first step. This guide breaks everything down into simple terms, so you know exactly what to expect and how to prepare.

Why Dubai is a Prime Choice for Investors

Dubai consistently ranks among the top global hubs for business and lifestyle. According to the Dubai Statistics Centre (2025), the emirate attracted over $10 billion in foreign direct investment (FDI) in 2024 alone, making it the top FDI destination globally for the third consecutive year.

Some key reasons investors choose Dubai include:

  • 100% business ownership in most sectors.
  • A strong infrastructure connecting businesses to global markets.
  • A safe and stable environment for families and businesses alike.

This growth-friendly ecosystem has made the Dubai investor visa an attractive option for entrepreneurs, property buyers, and business owners worldwide.

Understanding Investor Visa Cost in Dubai

The investor visa cost in Dubai varies depending on the type of investment and visa duration. Costs generally include application fees, medical testing, Emirates ID issuance, and other administrative charges.

On average, here’s what you can expect in 2025:

Visa Type Duration Approximate Cost (AED)
Investor Visa – Mainland Company 3 Years 4,000 – 6,000 AED
Investor Visa – Property Investment 2 Years 3,500 – 5,000 AED
Investor Visa – Free Zone Company 3 Years 4,500 – 6,500 AED

Note: These costs do not include the investment amount itself. For example, a property investor must purchase real estate worth at least AED 750,000 (as per 2025 UAE regulations) to be eligible.

Eligibility Criteria for a Dubai Investor Visa

Before applying, you must meet the specific eligibility requirements set by UAE authorities. These criteria vary depending on the type of investment.

1. Company Formation

  • Must own shares in an existing UAE company or set up a new business.
  • Minimum share capital requirements depend on the emirate and business activity.
  • Business must be registered with the Department of Economic Development (DED) or a free zone authority.

2. Property Investment

  • Must own property in Dubai worth at least AED 750,000 (2025 minimum).
  • Property must be ready for occupancy (off-plan properties are not eligible).
  • Ownership must be under your name (individual or joint ownership in specific cases).

3. Partnership in an Existing Company

  • Must hold shares or be an active partner.
  • The company’s trade license and MOA (Memorandum of Association) must reflect your role.

These requirements ensure that only genuine investors contribute to Dubai’s economy while enjoying residency benefits.

Required Documents for a Dubai Investor Visa

Document submission is a critical step in the application process. Providing accurate and complete paperwork helps avoid delays or rejection.

Common Documents for All Investor Visas

  • Valid passport (minimum 6 months validity).
  • Recent passport-size photographs.
  • Completed visa application form.
  • Medical fitness test results.
  • Emirates ID application form.

Additional Documents Based on Investment Type

For Company Investment:

  • Trade license copy.
  • Memorandum of Association (MOA).
  • Bank statement showing proof of capital.

For Property Investment:

  • Title deed issued by Dubai Land Department.
  • Property valuation certificate.
  • NOC (No Objection Certificate) from the developer if applicable.

For Partnership in Existing Business:

  • Share certificate.
  • Partnership contract attested by a notary.

Step-by-Step Process to Apply for a Dubai Investor Visa

Applying for a Dubai Investor Visa becomes much easier when you follow each stage in order. Below is the complete process from start to finish.

Choose the Right Investment Path

Decide whether your investment will be in property, a new business, or an existing company. Each option has its own eligibility requirements and minimum investment threshold. For example, property investors usually need a minimum property value of AED 750,000, while business investors often require higher capital.

Prepare the Required Documents

Collect all necessary documents before starting your application. Common requirements include a valid passport, recent photographs, proof of investment, trade license (for business investments), and your Emirates ID application form. Preparing them in advance prevents unnecessary delays.

Submit Your Visa Application

Once your documents are ready, submit your application to the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA) in Dubai or an approved typing center. Many investors choose to work with business setup consultancies like KPMPRO to handle paperwork and ensure compliance.

Pay the Applicable Fees

The cost of a Dubai Investor Visa varies depending on the type and validity period. On average, it ranges from AED 4,000 to AED 6,000 for a three-year visa, excluding medical tests and Emirates ID charges. Always keep payment receipts for reference.

Complete Medical Testing and Biometrics

Undergo a mandatory medical fitness test at a licensed health center in Dubai. This includes blood tests and X-rays. You’ll also need to submit biometric data (such as fingerprints) for your Emirates ID processing.

Receive Your Investor Visa

After approval, your investor visa will be stamped in your passport. This grants you the legal right to live in Dubai, manage your investments, and enjoy the benefits of long-term residency.

Dubai Investor Visa Cost: Comparing Mainland, Free Zone & Property Options

When evaluating Dubai investor visa cost, it’s essential to compare the three main options:

Criteria Mainland Company Free Zone Company Property Investment
Visa Validity 3 years 3 years 2 years
Cost Range 4,000–6,000 AED 4,500–6,500 AED 3,500–5,000 AED
Ownership 100% in most sectors 100% Full ownership of property
Processing Time 2–3 weeks 2–4 weeks 2–3 weeks

Your choice should depend on your investment goals, whether that’s expanding your business operations or securing long-term residency through property ownership.

Renewal & Maintenance of Your Dubai Investor Visa

Investor visas are not a one-time process; they require timely renewal to maintain your residency status.

  • Renewal Period: Every 2–3 years (depending on visa type).
  • Cost: Similar to initial application fees.
  • Requirements: Proof of continued investment and updated documents.

Failing to renew on time can result in fines or visa cancellation, so it’s essential to track your renewal dates.

Benefits of Holding a Dubai Investor Visa

An investor visa offers more than just residency — it opens the door to numerous opportunities:

Residency for Family

You can sponsor your spouse, children, and parents.

Ease of Travel

Multiple-entry visa allows free movement in and out of the UAE.

Business Expansion

Access to global markets through Dubai’s trade network.

Banking & Finance

Easier to open corporate and personal bank accounts.

These benefits make the cost of an investor visa in Dubai a worthwhile investment for those seeking long-term stability and growth.

Final Word

The investor visa cost in Dubai is an investment in both your business and lifestyle. With the right guidance, clear understanding of requirements, and timely document submission, securing your residency in one of the world’s most dynamic cities is entirely achievable.

FAQs:

What is an Investor Visa in Dubai?

The Dubai Investor Visa allows foreign investors to live and work in the UAE. They are also permitted to manage their business or property in the UAE.

How much does an Investor Visa cost in Dubai?

The Dubai investor visa costs between 3,500 and 6,500 Dirhams. However, the cost depends on your investment type and visa duration.

What are the eligibility criteria for a Dubai Investor Visa?

To obtain a Dubai investor visa, you must own a Dubai-based business or property worth at least 750,000 Dirhams. You should also meet specific UAE investment requirements.

Can I get a 10-year Investor Visa in Dubai?

Yes! Investors meeting the Golden Visa criteria with 2 million Dirhams in property can get a 10-year visa.

What documents are required for an Investor Visa application?

The documents you’ll need for an investor visa application are:

  • Passport
  • Photos
  • Proof of investment
  • Trade license or title deed, and
  • A medical fitness certificate.
